# Introduction

[Direct link to openapi.json](https://api.aiven.io/doc/openapi.json) for use with external tools

[Aiven](https://aiven.io) is a modern fully-managed open source data platform for streaming, storing, and analyzing data on any public cloud. On Aiven Platform, you can operate your data infrastructure with a few devops tools: [Aiven Console](https://console.aiven.io/), [Aiven Terraform Provider](https://aiven.io/docs/tools/terraform), [Aiven CLI](https://github.com/aiven/aiven-client), and [Aiven Operator for Kubernetes](https://github.com/aiven/aiven-operator). All of them are built on an open secure powerful REST API for integration with custom tooling.

The Aiven [REST](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer) API
provides programmatic access to Aiven.io services. To call the Aiven API, you can use either CLI tools (for example, `cURL` or [Aiven CLI client](https://aiven.io/docs/tools/cli)) or GUI tools, such as the [Aiven public API Postman collection](https://www.postman.com/aiven-apis).

This Aiven API documentation will help you operate your Aiven organization, projects, or services programmatically by integrating your applications and processes with Aiven.

# Description

Aiven's APIs ([Application Programming Interfaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API)) power its platform for data management. Aiven has a number of REST APIs that can help you build strong and robust data infrastructure for your applications.

The Aiven API is organized around core resources. Each core resource has multiple endpoints, which can be interacted with using different HTTP methods.

## Core resources

### Platform APIs

<dl>
  <dt>Account</dt>
  <dd>Operations on the organization level related to accounts, projects, user groups, users, invites, billing groups, payment methods, credit cards, authentication methods, and more </dd>
  <dt>User</dt>
  <dd>Operations related to users and users' profiles, access, authentication, authorization, user management, and more</dd>
  <dt>Project</dt>
  <dd>General operations on projects related to users, VPCs, invitations, alerts, peering connections, and more</dd>
  <dt>BillingGroup</dt>
  <dd>Operation on invoices, billing groups' credits and events </dd>
  <dt>Support ticket</dt>
  <dd>Operations on support tickets: listing, creating, looping users in</dd>
</dl>

### Services APIs

<dl>
  <dt>Service</dt>
  <dd>All general (non-service-specific) operations on the service level: service creation, termination, configuration, updates, information retrieval, reset, and more</dd>
  <dt>Service Integrations</dt>
  <dd>Operations related to integrating services and managing service integrations</dd>
  <dt>Service: ClickHouse</dt>
  <dd>ClickHouse-specific operations on queries and databases </dd>
  <dt>Service: Flink</dt>
  <dd>Operations on Flink queries, jobs, and applications</dd>
  <dt>Service: Kafka</dt>
  <dd>Kafka and Kafka Connect specific operations on connectors, ACL entries, quotas, topics, topic messages, schema registry, and more</dd>
  <dt>Service: Kafka MirrorMaker</dt>
  <dd>Operations on replication flows</dd>
  <dt>Service: MySQL</dt>
  <dd>Fetching service query statistics</dd>
  <dt>Service: OpenSearch</dt>
  <dd>Operations on ACL configuration, security administration and configuration</dd>
  <dt>Service: PostgreSQL</dt>
  <dd>Operations on extensions, service query statistics, and connection pools</dd>
</dl>

# Requests

There are multiple ways you can interact with the Aiven API over HTTP. You can access it by sending requests from a client (for example, a web browser) to the Aiven's server. In this API reference, you'll find code examples of how to do that using `cURL` and a few different client libraries (programming languages).

To send an API request, you need to specify the following:

* HTTP method
* Path
* Request headers

  Typically, `content-type` needs to be set to `application/json`: `content-type: application/json`. There are a few exceptions though.

* Path, query, or body parameters (either required or optional).

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.aiven.io/v1/project/{project}/vpcs \
  --header 'Authorization: aivenv1 REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data
     '{
        "cloud_name": "string",
        "network_cidr": "string",
        "peering_connections": [
          {
            "peer_azure_app_id": "string",
            "peer_azure_tenant_id": "string",
            "peer_cloud_account": "string",
            "peer_region": "string",
            "peer_resource_group": "string",
            "peer_vpc": "string",
            "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
              "string"
            ]
          }
        ]
      }'
```

# Responses

Upon receiving and processing a request, the Aiven API returns the response status code, response headers, and a response body in the `JSON` format. Response bodies include different properties, which can be either required or optional, for example, the ``message`` property, which is an optional human-readable information on the result of the action (deleted, created, or updated).

```json
{
    "cloud_name": "string",
    "create_time": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "network_cidr": "string",
    "peering_connections": [
        { ... }
    ],
    "pending_build_only_peering_connections": "string",
    "project_vpc_id": "string",
    "state": "ACTIVE",
    "update_time": "string"
}
```

## Successful responses

A successful API response returns an HTTP result code between 200 and 299.

Example of the ``created`` response

```json
  {
      "service": {
          "service_name": "foobar",
          ...
      }
  }
```

## Failed responses

A failed API response returns a HTTP code greater or equal to 400. Additionally, the response may return a list of errors in the response body as JSON, for example

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_code": "authentication_failed",
      "message": "Authentication failed",
      "status": 403,
      "metadata": {
        ...
      }
    }
  ],
  "message": "Authentication failed"
}
```

> For information on errors' properties and error codes, check [Errors](/doc/openapi/openapi-description#errors).

# Errors

When working with the Aiven API, you may encounter different error responses when you attempt to perform operations that can fail. For example, trying to enable writes for a database that has been powered off would lead to the following error response:

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_code": "not_powered",
      "message": "Database not powered on",
      "status": 409
    }
  ],
  "message": "Database not powered on"
}
```

## Check a response for errors

If a request fails with a HTTP code greater or equal to 400, it returns a list of errors in the response body as JSON. `errors` objects are embedded in the failed API responses.

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "error_code": "account_not_found",
      "message": "Account does not exist",
      "status": 404
    }
  ],
  "message": "Account does not exist"
}
```

## Errors' properties

In an API response, one or more errors may be included in the ``errors`` array of objects. Each error object may contain a few properties:

* ``status`` (required) is an HTTP error code, which can be used to programmatically identify the error type.

  * ``200`` <= ``status``< ``300`` means a successful request.
  * ``300`` <= ``status`` <= ``500`` means a failed request.

  ``errors`` can have the following HTTPS status codes:

  * 200 - OK
  * 201 - Created
  * 400 - Bad Request
  * 401 - Unauthorized
  * 403 - Forbidden
  * 404 - Not found
  * 405 - Method Not Allowed
  * 409 - Conflict
  * 500 - Internal Server Error

* ``message`` (required) is human-readable information on the error.
* ``error_code`` is a machine-readable information on the error (see [Error codes](/doc/openapi/openapi-description#error-codes)).

## Error codes

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Header should be of the format `authorization: aivenv1 <TOKEN>`. Tokens can be obtained from [your Aiven profile page](https://console.aiven.io/profile/auth)

- oAuth2 authentication. OAuth2 security scheme

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://console.aiven.io/oauth/authorize](https://console.aiven.io/oauth/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://api.aiven.io/v1/oauth2/token](https://api.aiven.io/v1/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|all|Provide full access to the API|
|accounts|Allow enumerating and reading accounts configuration|
|accounts:read|Allow modifying account configuration|
|accounts:write|Provides full access to authentication related API|
|authentication|Provides full access to authentication related API|
|authentication:read|Allow reading authentication related configuration on resources (user profile, accounts)|
|authentication:write|Allow modifying authentication related configurations on resources (user profile, accounts)|
|billing|Provide full access to billing APIs|
|billing:read|Allow reading billing information and configuration|
|billing:write|Allow writing billing configuration|
|payments|Provide full access to payment method APIs|
|payments:read|Allow reading the payment method configurations|
|payments:write|Allows writing payment method configuration|
|privatelink|Provide full access to private link APIs|
|privatelink:read|Allow enumerating and reading private link items and configurations|
|privatelink:write|Allow writing (creating, modifying, deleting) private link items|
|projects|Provide full access to projects APIs|
|projects:read|Allow enumerating projects and reading their configuration|
|projects:write|Allow writing (creating, modifying, deleting) projects|
|scim|Provide full access to SCIM operations|
|scim:read|Allow reading SCIM endpoints|
|scim:write|Allow writing (modifying) SCIM endpoints|
|services|Provide full access to services APIs|
|services:read|Allow enumerating services and reading their configuration|
|services:write|Allow writing (creating, modifying, deleting) services|
|static_ips|Provide full access to static IPs APIs|
|static_ips:read|Allow enumerating and reading static IP items and configurations|
|static_ips:write|Allow writing (creating, modifying, deleting) static IP items|
|user|Provide full access to user profile APIs|
|user:read|Allow reading user profile and configuration|
|user:write|Allow writing (modifying) user profile and configuration|

<h1 id="aiven-api-documentation-aigateway">AIGateway</h1>

## List the AI Gateway keys of a project

<a id="opIdAIGatewayKeyList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/ai-gateway/keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /project/{project}/ai-gateway/keys`

<p><blockquote>This endpoint <b>may be changed or removed at any time</b>. Don't use it in production environments.</blockquote><p>

<p>Expired keys are not listed, unless <code>include_expired</code> is set. Revoked keys are not listed, unless <code>include_revoked</code> is set. Keys are listed newest first and one page at a time; follow <code>next</code> until it comes back null to read the whole list.</p>

<h3 id="list-the-ai-gateway-keys-of-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|include_revoked|query|boolean|false|Also list revoked keys|


`GET /project/{project}/ai-gateway/usage`

<p><blockquote>This endpoint <b>may be changed or removed at any time</b>. Don't use it in production environments.</blockquote><p>

<p>A row with no <code>key_id</code> is the whole project's usage for that time bucket and model, and is reported only when no <code>key_id</code> is asked for. A bucket nothing was spent on is left out rather than reported as zeroes. Both ends of the range must fall on a UTC minute. A bucket that the range cuts holds only the usage inside the range. A range on whole UTC hours at hour or day granularity is read from the hourly totals, which keep the whole history but take up to about 15 minutes to show recent usage. Any other range is read from the requests themselves, which are up to date but kept for 3 months only. The cost is an estimate at the rates the catalogue lists now, not what was charged at the time: the input outside the prompt cache, the tokens read from and written to it, and the output, each at a rate of its own. A model the catalogue no longer lists keeps its usage and is reported with no cost at all.</p>

<h3 id="get-how-many-tokens-a-project-has-spent-on-the-ai-gateway-per-key-minute-hour-or-day-and-model-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|key_id|query|string|false|Report only this key, and no project totals|
|starting_time|query|string|false|Start of the range, inclusive, on a UTC minute (ISO 8601, default: start of the month)|
|ending_time|query|string|false|End of the range, exclusive, on a UTC minute (ISO 8601, default: the end of the current hour)|
|granularity|query|string|false|Size of the time buckets usage is reported in. A per-minute range is limited to 1 day, an hourly one to 7 days, a daily one to 366|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|granularity|minute|
|granularity|hour|
|granularity|day|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "usage": [
    {
      "cache_read_tokens": 0,
      "cache_write_tokens": 0,
      "estimated_cost_usd": 0,
      "input_tokens": 0,
      "key_id": "stringstringstringstringstringstring",
      "model_name": "string",
      "output_tokens": 0,
      "request_count": 0,
      "timestamp": "string",
      "total_tokens": 0,
      "uncached_input_tokens": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "feature_not_enabled"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [

      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "ai_gateway_key_not_found"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "ai_gateway_unavailable"
```

<h3 id="get-how-many-tokens-a-project-has-spent-on-the-ai-gateway-per-key-minute-hour-or-day-and-model-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[AIGatewayUsageGetResponse](#schemaaigatewayusagegetresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The granularity is not minute, hour or day, or the time range is unreadable, off the minute, reversed, longer than the maximum, older than the requests are kept for, or matches more usage than one response holds|Inline|

|404|Not Found|Key not found|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|The key cannot be looked up|Inline|

|» » email|body|string|false|Field name for user email|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's first name|
|» » groups|body|string|false|Field name for user's groups memberships. Contents of this field are used to handle group memberships when SCIM is not available and SAML is used to manage group memberships.|
|» » identity|body|string|false|Field name for user's identity. This field must always exist in responses, and must be immutable and unique. Contents of this field are used to identify the user. Using user ID (such as unix user ID) is highly recommended, as email address may change, requiring relinking user to Aiven user.|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's lastname|
|» » real_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's full name. If specified, first_name and last_name mappings are ignored|

|» saml_requested_authn_context_enabled|body|boolean|false|Set to 'false' to disable RequestedAuthnContext|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» saml_variant|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» scim_enabled|body|boolean|false|SCIM enabled|

```json
  },
```

```bash
  "saml_idp_url": "https://example.com/saml2/idp",
  "saml_join_groups": true,
```

```json
  "saml_signature_algorithm": "rsa-sha256",
  "saml_variant": "adfs",
  "scim_enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-authentication-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|Account ID|
|account_authentication_method_id|path|string|true|Account authentication method ID|
|body|body|[AccountAuthenticationMethodUpdateRequestBody](#schemaaccountauthenticationmethodupdaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» auth_token_extend_when_used|body|boolean|false|Extend authentication token validity when used|
|» auth_token_max_age_seconds|body|integer|false|Auth Token Max Age Seconds|
|» authentication_method_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, authentication method can be used to access account/projects in account. If false, authentication method can still be used to sign in|
|» authentication_method_name|body|string|false|Authentication Method Name|
|» auto_join_team_id|body|string|false|Deprecated; always null. Teams are being sunset, so this value is ignored on writes and always returned as null.|
|» auto_join_user_group_id|body|string|false|Automatically add users to a group, when user signs up using this authentication method|
|» saml_assertion_signed_enabled|body|boolean|false|Set to 'true' to enable WantAssertionsSigned|
|» saml_authn_requests_signed_enabled|body|boolean|false|Set to 'true' to enable AuthnRequestsSigned|
|» saml_certificate|body|string|false|Identity provider's certificate|
|» saml_digest_algorithm|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» saml_entity_id|body|string|false|Saml Entity ID|
|» saml_field_mapping|body|object|false|SAMLFieldMapping|
|» » email|body|string|false|Field name for user email|
|» » first_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's first name|
|» » groups|body|string|false|Field name for user's groups memberships. Contents of this field are used to handle group memberships when SCIM is not available and SAML is used to manage group memberships.|
|» » identity|body|string|false|Field name for user's identity. This field must always exist in responses, and must be immutable and unique. Contents of this field are used to identify the user. Using user ID (such as unix user ID) is highly recommended, as email address may change, requiring relinking user to Aiven user.|
|» » last_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's lastname|
|» » real_name|body|string|false|Field name for user's full name. If specified, first_name and last_name mappings are ignored|
|» saml_idp_login_allowed|body|boolean|false|Set to 'true' to enable IdP initiated login|
|» saml_idp_url|body|string|false|Saml Idp Url|
|» saml_join_groups|body|boolean|false|SAML join groups enabled|
|» saml_requested_authn_context_enabled|body|boolean|false|Set to 'false' to disable RequestedAuthnContext|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» saml_variant|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» scim_enabled|body|boolean|false|SCIM enabled|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» saml_digest_algorithm|sha1|
|» saml_digest_algorithm|sha256|
|» saml_digest_algorithm|sha384|
|» saml_digest_algorithm|sha512|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|rsa-sha1|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|dsa-sha1|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|rsa-sha256|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|rsa-sha384|
|» saml_signature_algorithm|rsa-sha512|
|» saml_variant|adfs|

## Create an application token

<a id="opIdApplicationUserAccessTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/application-users/string/access-tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Integration client Alpha",
    "extend_when_used": false,
    "ip_allowlist": [
      "192.168.0.0/24",
      "2001:db8::/32"
    ],
    "max_age_seconds": 86400,
    "scopes": [
      "user:read"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/application-users/{user_id}/access-tokens`

<p>Creates a token for an application user.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Integration client Alpha",
  "extend_when_used": false,
  "ip_allowlist": [
    "192.168.0.0/24",
    "2001:db8::/32"
  ],
  "max_age_seconds": 86400,
  "scopes": [
    "user:read"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-application-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|user_id|path|string|true|User ID|
|body|body|[ApplicationUserAccessTokenCreateRequestBody](#schemaapplicationuseraccesstokencreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|true|Description|
|» extend_when_used|body|boolean|false|Extend token expiration time when token is used. Only applicable if max_age_seconds is specified.|
|» ip_allowlist|body|[string]|false|List of allowed IP ranges|
|» max_age_seconds|body|integer|false|Time the token remains valid since creation (or since last use if extend_when_used is true)|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes this token is restricted to if specified|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Show fee breakdown for a billing group, aggregated by type of usage and/or service

<a id="opIdBillingGroupFeeBreakdownAggregate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/billing-group/string/fee-breakdown \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/{organization_id}/billing-group/{billing_group_id}/fee-breakdown`

<p>Returns the charges a billing group accrued over one calendar month, aggregated so that each entry covers all usage of a single item type. Charges that belong to a project are grouped per project under <code>project_charges</code>, each with the per-service entries that make it up; charges that apply to the billing group as a whole, such as commitment fees and minimum support fees, are listed under <code>non_project_charges</code>. <code>total_charges_usd</code> is the sum of both lists. The breakdown covers usage metered for billing through the billing group's marketplace subscription. For a billing group billed in another way the request still succeeds, but <code>total_charges_usd</code> is <code>0</code> and <code>project_charges</code> and <code>non_project_charges</code> are empty; that is a valid result, not an error. A breakdown can likewise be empty, or cover only part of the month, if the way a billing group is billed changes during the reported period. These charges are billed through the marketplace rather than invoiced by Aiven, so the marketplace remains the authoritative record of what is actually charged; contact Aiven if a month that should be covered here returns no charges. The reported month is selected with the <code>since</code> parameter: the period always starts at 00:00 UTC on the first day of the month containing <code>since</code> and ends at 00:00 UTC on the first day of the following month, so <code>period_begin</code> is inclusive and <code>period_end</code> is exclusive. Metering data from before 2024-10-01 is not available; when <code>since</code> falls in an earlier month the period collapses to an empty range and no charges are returned. A month is reported once the usage it contains has been through billing finalization. Usage that has not been finalized yet is left out, so the figures for the current month grow as the month progresses and only settle after it has closed. Amounts are in USD, given as decimal strings rather than numbers so that no precision is lost, and they are stated before tax and before credits are applied. They are therefore not expected to match the amount the marketplace bills for the same period. Charges are collected per month by selecting every metering record that overlaps the month, so an individual entry may cover usage that starts before <code>period_begin</code> or ends after <code>period_end</code>; the <code>period_begin</code> and <code>period_end</code> of each entry report the usage window that entry actually covers. Because of this, the totals here can differ from the non-aggregated records returned by <code>GET /v1/organization/{organization_id}/billing-group/{billing_group_id}/fee-breakdown/download</code>, which only includes records that fall entirely inside the month. Within an entry, <code>unit_price_usd</code> is the highest unit price seen among the aggregated charges, so <code>units</code> multiplied by <code>unit_price_usd</code> does not necessarily equal <code>item_price_usd</code>; <code>item_price_usd</code> is the authoritative amount. Sending an <code>Accept: text/csv</code> request header returns the same aggregated data as a CSV attachment instead of JSON. The CSV is flat, one row per aggregated entry, with the columns <code>project_name</code>, <code>item_type</code>, <code>total_units</code>, <code>unit_price_usd</code>, <code>item_total_price_usd</code>, <code>cloud_name</code>, <code>service_name</code>, <code>service_type</code>, <code>service_plan</code>, <code>usage_started_at</code> and <code>usage_finished_at</code>. <code>project_name</code> is empty for charges that are not tied to a project.</p>

<h3 id="show-fee-breakdown-for-a-billing-group-aggregated-by-type-of-usage-andor-service-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|billing_group_id|path|string|true|Billing group id|
|since|query|string|false|Any date and time within the month to report, in ISO 8601 format. A date without a time zone is interpreted as UTC. The breakdown always covers the whole calendar month containing this value. Defaults to the current month.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "billing_group_id": "stringstringstringstringstringstring",
  "non_project_charges": [
    {
      "item_price_usd": "string",
      "item_type": "service_usage",
      "period_begin": "string",
      "period_end": "string",
      "unit_price_usd": "string",
      "units": 0
    }
  ],
  "period_begin": "string",
  "period_end": "string",
  "project_charges": [
    {
      "project_name": "string",
      "service_charges": [
        {
          "cloud_name": "string",
          "item_price_usd": "string",
          "item_type": "service_usage",
          "period_begin": "string",
          "period_end": "string",
          "service_name": "string",
          "service_plan": "string",
```

## Download fee breakdown for a billing group in CSV format

<a id="opIdBillingGroupFeeBreakdownDownload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/billing-group/string/fee-breakdown/download \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/{organization_id}/billing-group/{billing_group_id}/fee-breakdown/download`

<p>Returns the individual metered charges a billing group accrued over one calendar month as a CSV attachment. Unlike <code>GET /v1/organization/{organization_id}/billing-group/{billing_group_id}/fee-breakdown</code>, which aggregates charges per item type, this endpoint returns one row per metered charge, including the discounts that were applied to it. The CSV covers usage metered for billing through the billing group's marketplace subscription. For a billing group billed in another way the request still succeeds, but the file contains only its header row; that is a valid result, not an error. A file can likewise be empty, or cover only part of the month, if the way a billing group is billed changes during the reported period. These charges are billed through the marketplace rather than invoiced by Aiven, so the marketplace remains the authoritative record of what is actually charged; contact Aiven if a month that should be covered here contains no rows. The reported month is selected with the <code>since</code> parameter: the period always starts at 00:00 UTC on the first day of the month containing <code>since</code> and ends at 00:00 UTC on the first day of the following month. Metering data from before 2024-10-01 is not available; when <code>since</code> falls in an earlier month the period collapses to an empty range and the CSV contains only its header row. A month is reported once the usage it contains has been through billing finalization. Usage that has not been finalized yet is left out, so the rows for the current month accumulate as the month progresses and only settle after it has closed. Amounts are in USD before tax and before credits are applied, and are therefore not expected to match the amount the marketplace bills for the same period. The response is a CSV attachment with the columns <code>billing_group_id</code>, <code>status</code>, <code>item_type</code>, <code>units</code>, <code>unit_price_usd</code>, <code>item_price_usd</code>, <code>cloud_name</code>, <code>project_name</code>, <code>service_name</code>, <code>service_type</code>, <code>service_plan</code>, <code>usage_duration</code> and <code>discounts</code>. <code>usage_duration</code> is a PostgreSQL timestamp range covering the charged usage, with the start included and the end excluded, and <code>discounts</code> is a list of the discounts applied to the charge. Columns that do not apply to a charge are empty, for example <code>project_name</code> and the service columns for charges that are not tied to a service. At most 100000 rows can be downloaded for one month. A billing group whose month exceeds that returns <code>too_many_records_to_download</code> rather than a truncated file; contact Aiven to obtain the full CSV.</p>

<h3 id="download-fee-breakdown-for-a-billing-group-in-csv-format-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|billing_group_id|path|string|true|Billing group id|
|since|query|string|false|Any date and time within the month to report, in ISO 8601 format. A date without a time zone is interpreted as UTC. The breakdown always covers the whole calendar month containing this value. Defaults to the current month.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "invalid_date_format"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "billing_group_not_found"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "too_many_records_to_download"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a custom cloud

<a id="opIdCustomCloudEnvironmentCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/custom-cloud-environments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cloud_provider": "aws",
    "cloud_region": "eu-west-1",
    "contact_emails": [
      {
        "email": "jane@example.com",
        "real_name": "Jane Smith",
        "role": "admin"
      }
    ],
    "deployment_model": "standard",
    "display_name": "byoc-cloud-prod-eu-west-1",
    "reserved_cidr": "192.168.6.0/24",
    "tags": {}
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/custom-cloud-environments`

```json
    }
```

<h1 id="aiven-api-documentation-kafkaconnectcustomplugins">Kafka_Connect_Custom_Plugins</h1>

## List custom connectors available in the organization

<a id="opIdKafkaConnectCustomConnectorsList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/kafka-connect/custom-connectors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/{organization_id}/kafka-connect/custom-connectors`

<p>Returns one entry per plugin_name, combining plugin metadata, the latest non-deleted file version (by semver), the distinct connector class types from that version, the total deployment_count across all versions (from user_config, synchronous), and the configuration_count of services actively running a connector class from this plugin (from service_state, collected asynchronously every ~15 minutes). Optionally filtered to a single plugin via plugin_name.</p>

<h3 id="list-custom-connectors-available-in-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|plugin_name|query|string|false|Filter results to a specific custom plugin|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "custom_connectors": [
    {
      "configuration_count": 0,
      "deployment_count": 0,
      "latest_version": "string",
      "plugin_class_types": [
        "string"
      ],
      "plugin_description": "string",
      "plugin_name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "permission_denied"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-custom-connectors-available-in-the-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[KafkaConnectCustomConnectorsListResponse](#schemakafkaconnectcustomconnectorslistresponse)|

## Initiate a custom plugin file upload

<a id="opIdKafkaConnectCustomPluginFileCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/kafka-connect/custom-plugin-files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content_type": "application/java-archive",
    "file_description": "Fixed memory leak in the MQTT source connector.",
    "plugin_description": "My custom connector bundle for stream processing.",
    "plugin_name": "my-custom-connectors",
    "plugin_version": "2.7.14",
    "service_type": "kafka_connect"
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/kafka-connect/custom-plugin-files`

<p>Creates an organization_custom_plugin_files record and returns a presigned S3 PUT URL the client must use to upload the JAR directly. Poll GET to check file_status until it reaches READY or FAILED.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content_type": "application/java-archive",
  "file_description": "Fixed memory leak in the MQTT source connector.",
```

## Get a list of invoices

<a id="opIdOrganizationBillingInvoiceList"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/invoices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organization/{organization_id}/invoices`

<p>Lists the invoices of an organization whose billing period overlaps the requested date range. The date range is always bounded, so leaving out <code>starting_date</code> and <code>ending_date</code> does not list every invoice of the organization. With neither given, the range defaults to the previous full calendar month: from the first day of the previous month to the first day of the current month, both inclusive. With only <code>starting_date</code> given, the range covers the one month starting from that date. With only <code>ending_date</code> given, it covers the one month ending at that date. With both given, the range is the period between them, and <code>ending_date</code> must be after <code>starting_date</code> or the request fails with <code>bad_request</code>.</p>

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|billing_group_ids|query|array|false|IDs of the billing_groups|
|state|query|array|false|refers to state of the invoice|
|starting_date|query|string|false|start of the invoice time period, default: start of last month|
|ending_date|query|string|false|end of the invoice time period, default: start of this month|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "invoices": [
    {
      "billing_group_id": "string",
      "create_time": "string",
      "currency": "AUD",
      "download_only": true,
      "due_date": "string",
      "invoice_number": "string",
      "invoice_period": {
        "begin_time": "string",
        "end_time": "string"
      },
      "issue_date": "string",
      "net": "string",
      "net_usd": "string",
      "organization_id": "string",
      "overdue": true,
      "state": "accrual",
      "total": "string",
      "total_usd": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "bad_request"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "organization_not_found"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-invoices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[OrganizationBillingInvoiceListResponse](#schemaorganizationbillinginvoicelistresponse)|

|404|Not Found|Resource not found|Inline|

## Create organization VPC

<a id="opIdOrganizationVpcCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/vpcs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "clouds": [
      {
        "cloud_name": "aws-eu-central-1",
        "network_cidr": "192.168.6.0/24"
      }
    ],
    "display_name": "My organization VPC",
    "peering_connections": [
      {
        "peer_azure_app_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
        "peer_azure_tenant_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
        "peer_cloud_account": "123456789012",
        "peer_region": "us-east-1",
        "peer_resource_group": "my-peered-rg",
        "peer_vpc": "vpc-2f09a348",
        "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
          "192.168.6.0/24"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/vpcs`

<p>Creates an organization VPC. This requires the manage-organization-networking permissions and can be also achieved using the Aiven Console, the Aiven CLI, or the Aiven Terraform Provider.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "clouds": [
    {
      "cloud_name": "aws-eu-central-1",
      "network_cidr": "192.168.6.0/24"
    }
  ],
  "display_name": "My organization VPC",
  "peering_connections": [
    {
      "peer_azure_app_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
      "peer_azure_tenant_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
      "peer_cloud_account": "123456789012",
      "peer_region": "us-east-1",
      "peer_resource_group": "my-peered-rg",
      "peer_vpc": "vpc-2f09a348",
      "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
        "192.168.6.0/24"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-organization-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|body|body|[OrganizationVpcCreateRequestBody](#schemaorganizationvpccreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» clouds|body|[object]|true|Clouds to create this VPC in|
|» » cloud_name|body|string|true|Target cloud|
|» » network_cidr|body|string|true|IPv4 network range CIDR|
|» display_name|body|string|false|User defined display name for this VPC|
|» peering_connections|body|[object]|true|List of peering connection requests for the VPC|
|» » peer_azure_app_id|body|string|false|Azure app registration id in UUID4 form that is allowed to create a peering to the peer vnet|
|» » peer_azure_tenant_id|body|string|false|Azure tenant id in UUID4 form|
|» » peer_cloud_account|body|string|true|AWS account ID, GCP project ID, Azure subscription ID of the peered VPC, or string &quot;upcloud&quot; for UpCloud peering connections|
|» » peer_region|body|string|false|The peer VPC's region on AWS. May be omitted or set to null if the peer is in the same region as the Aiven project VPC. Omit or set to null on GCP, Azure, or UpCloud.|
|» » peer_resource_group|body|string|false|Azure resource group name of the peered VPC|
|» » peer_vpc|body|string|true|AWS VPC ID, GCP VPC network name, Azure Virtual network name of the peered VPC, or UpCloud VPC ID|
|» » user_peer_network_cidrs|body|[string]|false|List of private IPv4 ranges to route through the peering connection|

`DELETE /organization/{organization_id}/vpc/{organization_vpc_id}`

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/vpc/{organization_vpc_id}/peering-connections`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "peer_azure_app_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",

  "peer_region": "us-east-1",

  "peer_vpc": "vpc-2f09a348",
  "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
    "192.168.6.0/24"
  ]
}
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/vpc/{organization_vpc_id}/peering-connections/refresh`

<p>Triggers an asynchronous refresh of the peering connection states for an organization VPC. Checks the state of the peering connections in the cloud provider and updates them in Aiven.       "\\*": "acme",

```bash
      "actor_user_id": "u1a2b3c4d5e",

    "event_types": [
      "organization_create",

    ],
    "from_time": "2026-06-15T10:00:00Z",
    "to_time": "2026-07-15T10:00:00Z"
  }'
```

```json
    "service_id": "my-service",
    "unit_id": "a3fd7a594e01"
  },
  "event_types": [
    "organization_create",

  ],
  "from_time": "2026-06-15T10:00:00Z",
  "to_time": "2026-07-15T10:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="download-platform-event-log-entries-as-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|[OrganizationEventLogsDownloadRequestBody](#schemaorganizationeventlogsdownloadrequestbody)|false|none|
|» asset_filters|body|object|false|Restrict results by asset ID, actor, or a free-text term. Named fields must all match; the '*' key matches a free-text term against several fields at once.|
|» » \|body|string|false|Case-insensitive. Opaque ids must match in full, other values match on any substring. Metadata matches values only, never keys. Must be between 3 and 256 characters. Combination with the other filters narrows the result set.|
|» » actor|body|string|false|Actor|
|» » actor_user_id|body|string|false|Actor User ID|
|» » billing_group_id|body|string|false|Billing Group ID|
|» » project_id|body|string|false|Project ID|
|» » service_id|body|string|false|Service ID|
|» » unit_id|body|string|false|Unit ID|
|» event_types|body|[string]|false|Restrict results to these event types. 'null' applies no filtering; an empty list returns no events.|
|» from_time|body|string|false|Start of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). Defaults to 30 days before now.|
|» to_time|body|string|false|End of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). If omitted, no upper time bound is applied.|

```json
      "message": "string",

    }
```

## Get the number of service log entries per severity in a time window, in total and per time bucket

<a id="opIdOrganizationServiceLogCountsGet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/project/string/service/string/logs/counts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from_time": "2026-04-23T10:00:00Z",
    "interval_seconds": 150,
    "severity": "warning",
    "to_time": "2026-04-23T11:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/project/{project_id}/service/{service_id}/logs/counts`

<p><blockquote>This endpoint <b>may be changed or removed at any time</b>. Don't use it in production environments.</blockquote><p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from_time": "2026-04-23T10:00:00Z",
  "interval_seconds": 150,
  "severity": "warning",
  "to_time": "2026-04-23T11:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="get-the-number-of-service-log-entries-per-severity-in-a-time-window-in-total-and-per-time-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|project_id|path|string|true|Project Id|
|service_id|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[OrganizationServiceLogCountsGetRequestBody](#schemaorganizationservicelogcountsgetrequestbody)|false|none|
|» from_time|body|string|false|Start of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). Cannot be in the future. Defaults to one hour before 'to_time' when set, otherwise one hour before now.|
|» interval_seconds|body|integer|false|Width of each time bucket in seconds, from 1 to 86400. Defaults to the time window split into 24 buckets, rounded up to whole seconds. A time window needing more than 300 buckets is rejected.|
|» severity|body|string|false|Filter to entries with severity at least as severe as this value.|
|» to_time|body|string|false|End of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). A later time than now is treated as now. Defaults to now.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» severity|emergency|
|» severity|alert|
|» severity|critical|
|» severity|error|
|» severity|warning|
|» severity|notice|
|» severity|info|
|» severity|debug|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "buckets": [
    {
      "counts": {
        "alert": 0,
        "critical": 0,
        "debug": 0,
        "emergency": 0,
        "error": 0,
        "info": 0,
        "notice": 0,
        "warning": 0
      },
      "start_time": "string"
    }
  ],
  "from_time": "string",
  "interval_seconds": 0,
  "to_time": "string",
  "totals": {
    "alert": 0,
```

```bash
  "from_time": "2026-04-23T10:00:00Z",
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|

|service_id|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[OrganizationServiceLogsGetRequestBody](#schemaorganizationservicelogsgetrequestbody)|false|none|
|» cursor|body|string|false|Pagination cursor from a previous response. The cursor already encodes the time range, severity and sort order, so it is mutually exclusive with 'from_time', 'to_time', 'severity' and 'order_by' ('limit' may still be supplied).|
|» from_time|body|string|false|Start of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). Cannot be in the future. Defaults to one hour before 'to_time' when set, otherwise one hour before now.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|Number of entries per page.|
|» order_by|body|string|false|Sort order in 'column:direction' form. Only 'log_time:asc' and 'log_time:desc' are supported. Defaults to 'log_time:desc'. Mutually exclusive with 'cursor'.|
|» severity|body|string|false|Filter to entries with severity at least as severe as this value.|
|» to_time|body|string|false|End of the time window (ISO 8601 UTC). A later time than now is treated as now. Defaults to now.|

## Set permissions

<a id="opIdPermissionsSet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/permissions/project/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "permissions": [
      {
        "permissions": [
          "read_only"
        ],
        "principal_id": "u12345",
        "principal_type": "user"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /organization/{organization_id}/permissions/{resource_type}/{resource_id}`

<p>Replaces permissions for a resource. The entries entry provided in the request body are applied, replacing all the previously defined permissions defined on the specified resource. Updates are not atomic (changes are computed and each are individually applied); if an error occurs, permissions may have been partially updated. They are however idempotent, so in case of transient errors it is possible to simply retry the request.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    {
      "permissions": [
        "read_only"
      ],
      "principal_id": "u12345",
      "principal_type": "user"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|resource_type|path|string|true|Resource type|
|resource_id|path|string|true|Resource Id|
|body|body|[PermissionsSetRequestBody](#schemapermissionssetrequestbody)|false|none|
|» permissions|body|[object]|true|List of roles to set|
|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of roles|
|» » principal_id|body|string|true|ID of the principal|
|» » principal_type|body|string|true|An enumeration.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resource_type|project|
|resource_type|organization|
|resource_type|organization_unit|
|» » principal_type|user|
|» » principal_type|user_group|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

## Update permissions

<a id="opIdPermissionsUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/permissions/project/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "operation": "set",
    "permissions": [
      {
        "permissions": [
          "read_only"
        ],
        "principal_id": "u12345",
        "principal_type": "user"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /organization/{organization_id}/permissions/{resource_type}/{resource_id}`

<p>Updates permissions for a resource. Each entry provided in the request body is applied, replacing the previous assignment for the target principal. To remove permission assignments an entry with an empty set of permissions must be provided. Updates are not atomic (each entry is individually applied); if an error occurs, permissions may have been partially updated. They are however idempotent, so in case of transient errors it is possible to simply retry the request.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "operation": "set",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "permissions": [
        "read_only"
      ],
      "principal_id": "u12345",
      "principal_type": "user"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|resource_type|path|string|true|Resource type|
|resource_id|path|string|true|Resource Id|
|body|body|[PermissionsUpdateRequestBody](#schemapermissionsupdaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» operation|body|string|false|An enumeration.|
|» permissions|body|[object]|true|List of roles to adjust|
|» » permissions|body|[string]|true|List of roles|
|» » principal_id|body|string|true|ID of the principal|
|» » principal_type|body|string|true|An enumeration.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resource_type|project|

## Create a VPC in a cloud for the project

<a id="opIdVpcCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/vpcs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cloud_name": "aws-eu-central-1",
    "network_cidr": "192.168.6.0/24",
    "peering_connections": [
      {
        "peer_azure_app_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
        "peer_azure_tenant_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
        "peer_cloud_account": "123456789012",
        "peer_region": "us-east-1",
        "peer_resource_group": "my-peered-rg",
        "peer_vpc": "vpc-2f09a348",
        "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
          "192.168.6.0/24"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/vpcs`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cloud_name": "aws-eu-central-1",
  "network_cidr": "192.168.6.0/24",
  "peering_connections": [
    {
      "peer_azure_app_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
      "peer_azure_tenant_id": "adcf7194-d877-4505-a47a-91fefd96e3b8",
      "peer_cloud_account": "123456789012",
      "peer_region": "us-east-1",
      "peer_resource_group": "my-peered-rg",
      "peer_vpc": "vpc-2f09a348",
      "user_peer_network_cidrs": [
        "192.168.6.0/24"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|body|body|[VpcCreateRequestBody](#schemavpccreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» cloud_name|body|string|true|Target cloud|
|» network_cidr|body|string|true|IPv4 network range CIDR|
|» peering_connections|body|[object]|true|List of peering connection requests for the VPC|
|» » peer_azure_app_id|body|string|false|Azure app registration id in UUID4 form that is allowed to create a peering to the peer vnet|

|» » peer_resource_group|body|string|false|Azure resource group name of the peered VPC|
|» » peer_vpc|body|string|true|AWS VPC ID, GCP VPC network name, Azure Virtual network name of the peered VPC, or UpCloud VPC ID|

## Check if the state of peering connections in the cloud has changed

<a id="opIdVpcPeeringConnectionsRefresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/vpcs/string/peering-connections/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /project/{project}/vpcs/{project_vpc_id}/peering-connections/refresh`

<p><blockquote>This endpoint <b>may be changed or removed at any time</b>. Don't use it in production environments.</blockquote><p>

<p>Triggers an asynchronous refresh of the peering connection states for a project VPC. Checks the state of the peering connections in the cloud provider and updates them in Aiven. To confirm the refresh has completed, retrieve the project VPC using <code>GET /project/{project}/vpcs/{project_vpc_id}</code> and check that the <code>pending_build_only_peering_connections</code> field has returned to <code>null</code>.</p>

```bash
    "application_version": {
      "sinks": [
        {
          "create_table": "CREATE TABLE table1 cpu FLOAT, node INT, cpu_percent INT, occurred_at TIMESTAMP_LTZ(3) WITH ()",
          "integration_id": "9865d88e-b397-452e-b8a3-d716d6f85f7e"
        }
      ],
```

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/acl \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "permission": "readwrite",
    "topic": "top*",
    "username": "admin*"
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/acl`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permission": "readwrite",
  "topic": "top*",
  "username": "admin*"
}
```

<h3 id="add-aiven-kafka-acl-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[ServiceKafkaAclAddRequestBody](#schemaservicekafkaacladdrequestbody)|false|none|
|» permission|body|string|true|Permission of an Aiven Kafka ACL entry, as opposed to a Kafka-native one.|
|» topic|body|string|true|Topic name pattern|
|» username|body|string|true|Username|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» permission|admin|
|» permission|read|
|» permission|readwrite|
|» permission|write|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "acl": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "permission": "admin",
      "topic": "string",
      "username": "string"
    }
  ],
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "service_acl_too_many"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-aiven-kafka-acl-entry-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[ServiceKafkaAclAddResponse](#schemaservicekafkaacladdresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request parameters|Inline|

<h3 id="add-aiven-kafka-acl-entry-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|
|» error_code|string|false|none|service_acl_too_many: Maximum number of service ACLs reached|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» error_code|service_acl_too_many|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
tokenAuth & oauth2 ( Scopes: services:write )
</aside>

## Check that a custom plugin file can be installed on a service without connector class conflicts

<a id="opIdServiceKafkaConnectValidateCustomPluginClasses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/validate-custom-plugin-classes \

  -d '{

  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/validate-custom-plugin-classes`

<p>Validates the <code>custom_plugins</code> configuration the service would have if the plugin file were installed on it: the file replaces any other version of the same plugin already configured and is added to the other configured plugins. ## Create Kafka quota

<a id="opIdServiceKafkaQuotaCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/quota \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client\\-id": "abc123",
    "consumer_byte_rate": "1048576",
    "producer_byte_rate": "1048576",
    "request_percentage": "25",
    "user": "alice"
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/quota`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client\\-id": "abc123",
  "consumer_byte_rate": "1048576",
  "producer_byte_rate": "1048576",
  "request_percentage": "25",
  "user": "alice"
}
```

<h3 id="create-kafka-quota-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[ServiceKafkaQuotaCreateRequestBody](#schemaservicekafkaquotacreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» client\-id|body|string|false|Represents a logical group of clients, assigned a unique name by the client application. Quotas can be applied based on user, client-id, or both. The most relevant quota is chosen for each connection. All connections within a quota group share the same quota.|
|» consumer_byte_rate|body|number|false|Defines the bandwidth limit in bytes/sec for each group of clients sharing a quota. Every distinct client group is allocated a specific quota, as defined by the cluster, on a per-broker basis. Exceeding this limit results in client throttling.|
|» producer_byte_rate|body|number|false|Defines the bandwidth limit in bytes/sec for each group of clients sharing a quota. Every distinct client group is allocated a specific quota, as defined by the cluster, on a per-broker basis. Exceeding this limit results in client throttling.|
|» request_percentage|body|number|false|Sets the maximum percentage of CPU time that a client group can use on request handler I/O and network threads per broker within a quota window. Exceeding this limit triggers throttling. The quota, expressed as a percentage, also indicates the total allowable CPU usage for the client groups sharing the quota.|
|» user|body|string|false|Represents a logical group of clients, assigned a unique name by the client application. Quotas can be applied based on user, client-id, or both. The most relevant quota is chosen for each connection. All connections within a quota group share the same quota.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "more_info": "string",
      "status": 0
    }
  ],
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Get the Kafka tiered storage object storage usage by topic

<a id="opIdServiceKafkaTieredStorageStorageUsageByTopic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/kafka/tiered-storage/storage-usage/by-topic \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Create a Kafka topic

<a id="opIdServiceKafkaTopicCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/topic \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cleanup_policy": "delete",
    "config": {
      "cleanup_policy": "delete",
      "compression_type": "zstd",
      "delete_retention_ms": 0,
      "diskless_enable": false,
      "file_delete_delay_ms": 0,
      "flush_messages": 0,
      "flush_ms": 0,
      "index_interval_bytes": 0,
      "local_retention_bytes": -2,
      "local_retention_ms": -2,
      "max_compaction_lag_ms": 0,
      "max_message_bytes": 0,
      "message_downconversion_enable": true,
      "message_format_version": "2.7-IV2",
      "message_timestamp_after_max_ms": 0,
      "message_timestamp_before_max_ms": 0,
      "message_timestamp_difference_max_ms": 0,
      "message_timestamp_type": "CreateTime",
      "min_cleanable_dirty_ratio": 0.5,
      "min_compaction_lag_ms": 0,
      "min_insync_replicas": 2,
      "preallocate": false,
      "remote_storage_enable": false,
      "retention_bytes": -1,
      "retention_ms": 604800000,
      "segment_bytes": 1073741824,
      "segment_index_bytes": 0,
      "segment_jitter_ms": 0,
      "segment_ms": 1,
      "unclean_leader_election_enable": false
    },
    "min_insync_replicas": 2,
    "owner_user_group_id": "ug22ba494e096",
    "partitions": 1,
    "replication": 2,
    "retention_bytes": -1,
    "retention_hours": 72,
    "tags": [
      {
        "key": "My-tag_key",
        "value": "My tag value, value."
      }
    ],
    "topic_description": "Platform events",
    "topic_name": "mytopic"
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-a-kafka-topic-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[ServiceKafkaTopicCreateRequestBody](#schemaservicekafkatopiccreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» cleanup_policy|body|string|false|The retention policy to use on old segments. Possible values include 'delete', 'compact', or a comma-separated list of them. The default policy ('delete') will discard old segments when their retention time or size limit has been reached. The 'compact' setting will enable log compaction on the topic.|
|» config|body|object|false|Kafka topic configuration|
|» » cleanup_policy|body|string|false|The retention policy to use on old segments. Possible values include 'delete', 'compact', or a comma-separated list of them. The default policy ('delete') will discard old segments when their retention time or size limit has been reached. The 'compact' setting will enable log compaction on the topic.|
|» » compression_type|body|string|false|Specify the final compression type for a given topic. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'uncompressed' which is equivalent to no compression; and 'producer' which means retain the original compression codec set by the producer.|
|» » delete_retention_ms|body|integer|false|The amount of time to retain delete tombstone markers for log compacted topics. This setting also gives a bound on the time in which a consumer must complete a read if they begin from offset 0 to ensure that they get a valid snapshot of the final stage (otherwise delete tombstones may be collected before they complete their scan).|
|» » diskless_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether diskless should be enabled. This is only available for BYOC services with Diskless feature enabled.|
|» » file_delete_delay_ms|body|integer|false|The time to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem.|
|» » flush_messages|body|integer|false|This setting allows specifying an interval at which we will force an fsync of data written to the log. For example if this was set to 1 we would fsync after every message; if it were 5 we would fsync after every five messages. In general we recommend you not set this and use replication for durability and allow the operating system's background flush capabilities as it is more efficient.|
|» » flush_ms|body|integer|false|This setting allows specifying a time interval at which we will force an fsync of data written to the log. For example if this was set to 1000 we would fsync after 1000 ms had passed. In general we recommend you not set this and use replication for durability and allow the operating system's background flush capabilities as it is more efficient.|
|» » index_interval_bytes|body|integer|false|This setting controls how frequently Kafka adds an index entry to its offset index. The default setting ensures that we index a message roughly every 4096 bytes. More indexing allows reads to jump closer to the exact position in the log but makes the index larger. You probably don't need to change this.|
|» » local_retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum bytes tiered storage will retain segment files locally before it will discard old log segments to free up space. If set to -2, the limit is equal to overall retention time. If set to -1, no limit is applied but it's possible only if overall retention is also -1.|
|» » local_retention_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum time tiered storage will retain segment files locally before it will discard old log segments to free up space. If set to -2, the time limit is equal to overall retention time. If set to -1, no time limit is applied but it's possible only if overall retention is also -1.|
|» » max_compaction_lag_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum time a message will remain ineligible for compaction in the log. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted.|
|» » max_message_bytes|body|integer|false|The largest record batch size allowed by Kafka (after compression if compression is enabled). If this is increased and there are consumers older than 0.10.2, the consumers' fetch size must also be increased so that the they can fetch record batches this large. In the latest message format version, records are always grouped into batches for efficiency. In previous message format versions, uncompressed records are not grouped into batches and this limit only applies to a single record in that case.|
|» » message_downconversion_enable|body|boolean|false|This configuration controls whether down-conversion of message formats is enabled to satisfy consume requests. When set to false, broker will not perform down-conversion for consumers expecting an older message format. The broker responds with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION error for consume requests from such older clients. This configuration does not apply to any message format conversion that might be required for replication to followers.|
|» » message_format_version|body|string|false|Specify the message format version the broker will use to append messages to the logs. The value should be a valid ApiVersion. Some examples are: 0.8.2, 0.9.0.0, 0.10.0, check ApiVersion for more details. By setting a particular message format version, the user is certifying that all the existing messages on disk are smaller or equal than the specified version. Setting this value incorrectly will cause consumers with older versions to break as they will receive messages with a format that they don't understand. Deprecated in Kafka 4.0+: this configuration is removed and any supplied value will be ignored; for services upgraded to 4.0+, the returned value may be 'None'.|
|» » message_timestamp_after_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. Applies only for messages with timestamps later than the broker's timestamp.|
|» » message_timestamp_before_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. Applies only for messages with timestamps earlier than the broker's timestamp.|
|» » message_timestamp_difference_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. This configuration is ignored if message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime.|
|» » message_timestamp_type|body|string|false|Define whether the timestamp in the message is message create time or log append time.|
|» » min_cleanable_dirty_ratio|body|number|false|This configuration controls how frequently the log compactor will attempt to clean the log (assuming log compaction is enabled). By default we will avoid cleaning a log where more than 50% of the log has been compacted. This ratio bounds the maximum space wasted in the log by duplicates (at 50% at most 50% of the log could be duplicates). A higher ratio will mean fewer, more efficient cleanings but will mean more wasted space in the log. If the max.compaction.lag.ms or the min.compaction.lag.ms configurations are also specified, then the log compactor considers the log to be eligible for compaction as soon as either: (i) the dirty ratio threshold has been met and the log has had dirty (uncompacted) records for at least the min.compaction.lag.ms duration, or (ii) if the log has had dirty (uncompacted) records for at most the max.compaction.lag.ms period.|
|» » min_compaction_lag_ms|body|integer|false|The minimum time a message will remain uncompacted in the log. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted.|
|» » min_insync_replicas|body|integer|false|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|» » preallocate|body|boolean|false|True if we should preallocate the file on disk when creating a new log segment.|
|» » remote_storage_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether tiered storage should be enabled. This is only available for services with Tiered Storage feature enabled.|
|» » retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|» » retention_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum time we will retain a log before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. This represents an SLA on how soon consumers must read their data. If set to -1, no time limit is applied.|
|» » segment_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the segment file size for the log. Retention and cleaning is always done a file at a time so a larger segment size means fewer files but less granular control over retention. Setting this to a very low value has consequences, and the Aiven management plane ignores values less than 10 megabytes.|
|» » segment_index_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the size of the index that maps offsets to file positions. We preallocate this index file and shrink it only after log rolls. You generally should not need to change this setting.|
|» » segment_jitter_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum random jitter subtracted from the scheduled segment roll time to avoid thundering herds of segment rolling|
|» » segment_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the period of time after which Kafka will force the log to roll even if the segment file isn't full to ensure that retention can delete or compact old data. Setting this to a very low value has consequences, and the Aiven management plane ignores values less than 10 seconds.|
|» » unclean_leader_election_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether to enable replicas not in the ISR set to be elected as leader as a last resort, even though doing so may result in data loss.|
|» min_insync_replicas|body|integer|false|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|» owner_user_group_id|body|string|false|The user group that owns this topic|
|» partitions|body|integer|false|Number of partitions|
|» replication|body|integer|false|Number of replicas|
|» retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|» retention_hours|body|integer|false|DEPRECATED: use config.retention_ms|
|» tags|body|[object]|false|Topic tags|
|» » key|body|string|true|Tag key|
|» » value|body|string|true|Tag value|
|» topic_description|body|string|false|Topic description|
|» topic_name|body|string|true|Topic name|
