<h3 id="update-a-kafka-topic-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|topic_name|path|string|true|Kafka topic name|
|body|body|[ServiceKafkaTopicUpdateRequestBody](#schemaservicekafkatopicupdaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» config|body|object|false|Kafka topic configuration|
|» » cleanup_policy|body|string|false|The retention policy to use on old segments. Possible values include 'delete', 'compact', or a comma-separated list of them. The default policy ('delete') will discard old segments when their retention time or size limit has been reached. The 'compact' setting will enable log compaction on the topic.|
|» » compression_type|body|string|false|Specify the final compression type for a given topic. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'uncompressed' which is equivalent to no compression; and 'producer' which means retain the original compression codec set by the producer.|
|» » delete_retention_ms|body|integer|false|The amount of time to retain delete tombstone markers for log compacted topics. This setting also gives a bound on the time in which a consumer must complete a read if they begin from offset 0 to ensure that they get a valid snapshot of the final stage (otherwise delete tombstones may be collected before they complete their scan).|
|» » diskless_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether diskless should be enabled. This is only available for BYOC services with Diskless feature enabled.|
|» » file_delete_delay_ms|body|integer|false|The time to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem.|
|» » flush_messages|body|integer|false|This setting allows specifying an interval at which we will force an fsync of data written to the log. For example if this was set to 1 we would fsync after every message; if it were 5 we would fsync after every five messages. In general we recommend you not set this and use replication for durability and allow the operating system's background flush capabilities as it is more efficient.|
|» » flush_ms|body|integer|false|This setting allows specifying a time interval at which we will force an fsync of data written to the log. For example if this was set to 1000 we would fsync after 1000 ms had passed. In general we recommend you not set this and use replication for durability and allow the operating system's background flush capabilities as it is more efficient.|
|» » index_interval_bytes|body|integer|false|This setting controls how frequently Kafka adds an index entry to its offset index. The default setting ensures that we index a message roughly every 4096 bytes. More indexing allows reads to jump closer to the exact position in the log but makes the index larger. You probably don't need to change this.|
|» » local_retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum bytes tiered storage will retain segment files locally before it will discard old log segments to free up space. If set to -2, the limit is equal to overall retention time. If set to -1, no limit is applied but it's possible only if overall retention is also -1.|
|» » local_retention_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum time tiered storage will retain segment files locally before it will discard old log segments to free up space. If set to -2, the time limit is equal to overall retention time. If set to -1, no time limit is applied but it's possible only if overall retention is also -1.|
|» » max_compaction_lag_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum time a message will remain ineligible for compaction in the log. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted.|
|» » max_message_bytes|body|integer|false|The largest record batch size allowed by Kafka (after compression if compression is enabled). If this is increased and there are consumers older than 0.10.2, the consumers' fetch size must also be increased so that the they can fetch record batches this large. In the latest message format version, records are always grouped into batches for efficiency. In previous message format versions, uncompressed records are not grouped into batches and this limit only applies to a single record in that case.|
|» » message_downconversion_enable|body|boolean|false|This configuration controls whether down-conversion of message formats is enabled to satisfy consume requests. When set to false, broker will not perform down-conversion for consumers expecting an older message format. The broker responds with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION error for consume requests from such older clients. This configuration does not apply to any message format conversion that might be required for replication to followers.|
|» » message_format_version|body|string|false|Specify the message format version the broker will use to append messages to the logs. The value should be a valid ApiVersion. Some examples are: 0.8.2, 0.9.0.0, 0.10.0, check ApiVersion for more details. By setting a particular message format version, the user is certifying that all the existing messages on disk are smaller or equal than the specified version. Setting this value incorrectly will cause consumers with older versions to break as they will receive messages with a format that they don't understand. Deprecated in Kafka 4.0+: this configuration is removed and any supplied value will be ignored; for services upgraded to 4.0+, the returned value may be 'None'.|
|» » message_timestamp_after_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. Applies only for messages with timestamps later than the broker's timestamp.|
|» » message_timestamp_before_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. Applies only for messages with timestamps earlier than the broker's timestamp.|
|» » message_timestamp_difference_max_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message. If message.timestamp.type=CreateTime, a message will be rejected if the difference in timestamp exceeds this threshold. This configuration is ignored if message.timestamp.type=LogAppendTime.|
|» » message_timestamp_type|body|string|false|Define whether the timestamp in the message is message create time or log append time.|
|» » min_cleanable_dirty_ratio|body|number|false|This configuration controls how frequently the log compactor will attempt to clean the log (assuming log compaction is enabled). By default we will avoid cleaning a log where more than 50% of the log has been compacted. This ratio bounds the maximum space wasted in the log by duplicates (at 50% at most 50% of the log could be duplicates). A higher ratio will mean fewer, more efficient cleanings but will mean more wasted space in the log. If the max.compaction.lag.ms or the min.compaction.lag.ms configurations are also specified, then the log compactor considers the log to be eligible for compaction as soon as either: (i) the dirty ratio threshold has been met and the log has had dirty (uncompacted) records for at least the min.compaction.lag.ms duration, or (ii) if the log has had dirty (uncompacted) records for at most the max.compaction.lag.ms period.|
|» » min_compaction_lag_ms|body|integer|false|The minimum time a message will remain uncompacted in the log. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted.|
|» » min_insync_replicas|body|integer|false|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|» » preallocate|body|boolean|false|True if we should preallocate the file on disk when creating a new log segment.|
|» » remote_storage_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether tiered storage should be enabled. This is only available for services with Tiered Storage feature enabled.|
|» » retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|» » retention_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum time we will retain a log before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. This represents an SLA on how soon consumers must read their data. If set to -1, no time limit is applied.|
|» » segment_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the segment file size for the log. Retention and cleaning is always done a file at a time so a larger segment size means fewer files but less granular control over retention. Setting this to a very low value has consequences, and the Aiven management plane ignores values less than 10 megabytes.|
|» » segment_index_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the size of the index that maps offsets to file positions. We preallocate this index file and shrink it only after log rolls. You generally should not need to change this setting.|
|» » segment_jitter_ms|body|integer|false|The maximum random jitter subtracted from the scheduled segment roll time to avoid thundering herds of segment rolling|
|» » segment_ms|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the period of time after which Kafka will force the log to roll even if the segment file isn't full to ensure that retention can delete or compact old data. Setting this to a very low value has consequences, and the Aiven management plane ignores values less than 10 seconds.|
|» » unclean_leader_election_enable|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether to enable replicas not in the ISR set to be elected as leader as a last resort, even though doing so may result in data loss.|
|» min_insync_replicas|body|integer|false|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|» owner_user_group_id|body|string|false|The user group that owns this topic|
|» partitions|body|integer|false|Number of partitions|
|» replication|body|integer|false|Number of replicas|
|» retention_bytes|body|integer|false|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|» retention_hours|body|integer|false|DEPRECATED: use config.retention_ms|
|» tags|body|[object]|false|Topic tags|
|» » key|body|string|true|Tag key|
|» » value|body|string|true|Tag value|
|» topic_description|body|string|false|Topic description|

<h3 id="create-a-replication-flow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[ServiceKafkaMirrorMakerCreateReplicationFlowRequestBody](#schemaservicekafkamirrormakercreatereplicationflowrequestbody)|false|none|
|» config_properties_exclude|body|string|false|A comma separated list of topic configuration properties and/or regexes that should not be replicated. If omitted, MirrorMaker will use default list of exclusions. For stability reasons, we always include the unclean.leader.election.enable field in the excluded parameters. If you have specific requirements for this configuration, please reach out to our support team for assistance.|
|» diskless_az_enabled|body|boolean|false|Adds a diskless_az= hint to the replication flow's Kafka client.id so that diskless Kafka clusters serve the flow from brokers in the same availability zone.|
|» emit_backward_heartbeats_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to emit heartbeats to the direction opposite to the flow, i.e. to the source cluster|
|» emit_heartbeats_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to emit heartbeats to the target cluster|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Is replication flow enabled|
|» exactly_once_delivery_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to enable exactly-once message delivery. We recommend you set this to enabled for new replications.|
|» follower_fetching_enabled|body|boolean|false|Assigns a Rack ID based on the availability-zone to enable follower fetching and rack awareness per replication flow.|
|» offset_lag_max|body|integer|false|How out-of-sync a remote partition can be before it is resynced (default: 100)|
|» offset_syncs_topic_location|body|string|false|The location of the offset-syncs topic|
|» replication_factor|body|integer|false|Replication factor used when creating the remote topics. If the replication factor surpasses the number of nodes in the target cluster, topic creation will fail.|
|» replication_policy_class|body|string|false|Class which defines the remote topic naming convention|
|» source_cluster|body|string|true|The alias of the source cluster to use in this replication flow. Can contain the following symbols: ASCII alphanumerics, '.', '_', and '-'.|
|» sync_group_offsets_enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether to periodically write the translated offsets of replicated consumer groups (in the source cluster) to __consumer_offsets topic in target cluster, as long as no active consumers in that group are connected to the target cluster|
|» sync_group_offsets_interval_seconds|body|integer|false|Frequency at which consumer group offsets are synced (default: 60, every minute)|
|» target_cluster|body|string|true|The alias of the target cluster to use in this replication flow. Can contain the following symbols: ASCII alphanumerics, '.', '_', and '-'.|
|» topics|body|[string]|false|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should be replicated. MirrorMaker will replicate these topics if they are not matched by &quot;topics.exclude&quot;. Currently defaults to [&quot;.*&quot;].|
|» topics.blacklist|body|[string]|false|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|
|» topics.exclude|body|[string]|false|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|
|» topics_exclude|body|[string]|false|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» offset_syncs_topic_location|source|
|» offset_syncs_topic_location|target|
|» replication_policy_class|org.apache.kafka.connect.mirror.DefaultReplicationPolicy|
|» replication_policy_class|org.apache.kafka.connect.mirror.IdentityReplicationPolicy|

```json
      "message": "string",

    }
  ],

}
```

## Send a message to an agent within a session

<a id="opIdManagedAgentsMessageSend"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/project/string/managed-agents/agent/string/session/string/message \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "environment": "managed-agents-a1b2c3d4",
    "message": "Hello!",
    "stream": false
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/project/{project}/managed-agents/agent/{agent_id}/session/{session_id}/message`

<p><blockquote>This endpoint <b>may be changed or removed at any time</b>. Don't use it in production environments.</blockquote><p>

<p>When <code>stream</code> is set, the runtime's response is proxied to the client as Server-Sent Events. Streaming relies on a rapu-level passthrough; a runtime-agnostic redesign is tracked separately (deferred-streaming). Note for generated clients: the declared response schema describes the <code>stream: false</code> body only. OpenAPI here cannot express a streamed response, so with <code>stream: true</code> the actual response is <code>text/event-stream</code>: <code>data:</code>-prefixed JSON frames terminated by a <code>data: [DONE]</code> sentinel, with <code>: heartbeat</code> comment frames roughly every 15s to keep proxies from closing an idle connection (see <code>avn.rapu.sse_streaming</code>). The status commits to 200 before the first frame, so a late failure arrives in-band as an <code>error</code> event, not as an HTTP error. Console code must therefore take only the <strong>request</strong> type from the generated client for this endpoint and never its response type.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment": "managed-agents-a1b2c3d4",
  "message": "Hello!",
  "stream": false
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-message-to-an-agent-within-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|agent_id|path|string|true|Managed agent ID|
|session_id|path|string|true|Conversation session ID|
|body|body|[ManagedAgentsMessageSendRequestBody](#schemamanagedagentsmessagesendrequestbody)|false|none|
|» environment|body|string|false|Ignored today; the project's environment is resolved server-side.|
|» message|body|string|true|User message text|
|» stream|body|boolean|false|Stream the response as Server-Sent Events|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {
      "created_at": "string",
      "message_type": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "role": "string",
      "tool_call": {},
      "tool_return": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "request_forbidden"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Restore a snapshot from custom repository

<a id="opIdServiceOpensearchCustomRepoRestoreSnapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/opensearch/_snapshot/string/string/_restore \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ignore_index_settings": "index.number_of_replicas",
    "ignore_unavailable": false,
    "include_aliases": false,
    "include_global_state": false,
    "index_settings": "index.number_of_replicas=1",
    "indices": "*",
    "partial": false,
    "rename_alias_pattern": "(.+)",
    "rename_alias_replacement": "$1_restored",
    "rename_pattern": "(.+)",
    "rename_replacement": "$1_restored"
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/opensearch/_snapshot/{repository_name}/{snapshot_name}/_restore`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ignore_index_settings": "index.number_of_replicas",
  "ignore_unavailable": false,
  "include_aliases": false,
  "include_global_state": false,
  "index_settings": "index.number_of_replicas=1",
  "indices": "*",
  "partial": false,
  "rename_alias_pattern": "(.+)",
  "rename_alias_replacement": "$1_restored",
  "rename_pattern": "(.+)",
  "rename_replacement": "$1_restored"
}
```

<h3 id="restore-a-snapshot-from-custom-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|repository_name|path|string|true|Repository name|
|snapshot_name|path|string|true|Snapshot name|
|body|body|[ServiceOpensearchCustomRepoRestoreSnapshotRequestBody](#schemaserviceopensearchcustomreporestoresnapshotrequestbody)|false|none|
|» ignore_index_settings|body|string|false|Comma-delimited list of index settings to ignore|
|» ignore_unavailable|body|boolean|false|Ignore indices that are missing or closed|
|» include_aliases|body|boolean|false|Include aliases|
|» include_global_state|body|boolean|false|Restore global state|
|» index_settings|body|string|false|Comma-delimited list of index settings to override.|
|» indices|body|string|true|Comma-separated list of index patterns to restore|
|» partial|body|boolean|false|Allows to restore snapshot of indices with unavailable shards|
|» rename_alias_pattern|body|string|false|Rename pattern for aliases|
|» rename_alias_replacement|body|string|false|Rename replacement for aliases|
|» rename_pattern|body|string|false|Rename pattern for indices|

## Get query optimization recommendations for a query

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "do_not_store": true,
    "flags": [],
    "pg_version": "16",
    "query": "Select email from users;",
    "schema_metadata": "{ '\''columns'\'': [...], '\''indexes'\'': [...], '\''views'\'': [...], ... }"
  }'
```

## List service versions

<a id="opIdListServiceVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/service_versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /service_versions`

<h3 id="list-service-versions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|visible_until|query|string|false|How far into a version's lifecycle it should still be listed: end-of-availability (default, matches historical behavior), or end-of-life (Aiven's own end of life).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|visible_until|end-of-availability|
|visible_until|end-of-life|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "more_info": "string",
      "status": 0
    }
  ],

  "service_versions": [
    {
      "aiven_end_of_life_time": "string",
      "availability_end_time": "string",
      "availability_start_time": "string",
      "end_of_life_help_article_url": "string",
      "major_version": "string",
      "service_type": "string",
      "state": "available",
      "termination_time": "string",
      "upgrade_to_service_type": "string",
      "upgrade_to_version": "string",
      "upstream_end_of_life_time": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get service log entries

<a id="opIdProjectGetServiceLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/logs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "limit": 100,
    "log_type": "application-run",
    "offset": "23425325",
    "severity": "warning",
    "sort_order": "asc"
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/logs`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "limit": 100,
  "log_type": "application-run",
  "offset": "23425325",
  "severity": "warning",
  "sort_order": "asc"
}
```

<h3 id="get-service-log-entries-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[ProjectGetServiceLogsRequestBody](#schemaprojectgetservicelogsrequestbody)|false|none|
|» limit|body|integer|false|How many log entries to receive at most|
|» log_type|body|string|false|Filter to entries of a specific application log type. Only supported for application services. When omitted on application services, runtime logs (application-run) are returned.|
|» offset|body|string|false|Opaque offset identifier|
|» severity|body|string|false|Filter to entries with severity at least as severe as this value|
|» sort_order|body|string|false|Sort order for log messages|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» log_type|application-build|
|» log_type|application-run|
|» severity|emerg|
|» severity|alert|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|body|body|[ServiceCreateRequestBody](#schemaservicecreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» cloud|body|string|false|Target cloud|
|» cmk_id|body|string|false|Customer Managed Key identifier (CMK ID)|
|» copy_tags|body|boolean|false|If this is a forked service, copy tags from the source service. If request contains additional tags, the tags copied from source are updated with them.|
|» disk_space_mb|body|integer|false|Megabytes of disk space for data storage|
|» group_name|body|string|false|Service group name (DEPRECATED: do not use)|
|» maintenance|body|object|false|Automatic maintenance settings|
|» » dow|body|string|false|Day of week for installing updates|
|» » time|body|string|false|Time for installing updates, UTC|
|» plan|body|string|true|Subscription plan|
|» project_vpc_id|body|string|false|Project VPC ID|
|» service_integrations|body|[object]|false|Service integrations to enable for the service. Some integration types affect how a service is created and they must be provided as part of the creation call instead of being defined later.|
|» » dest_endpoint_id|body|string|false|Integration destination endpoint ID|
|» » dest_project|body|string|false|Defaults to project in the request path|
|» » dest_service|body|string|false|Destination service name|
|» » integration_type|body|string|true|Service integration type|
|» » source_endpoint_id|body|string|false|Integration source endpoint ID|

## Rotate DataHub internal authentication secrets

<a id="opIdServiceDataHubRotateInternalSecrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/rotate-internal-secrets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/rotate-internal-secrets`

<p>Generates fresh values for DATAHUB_SECRET (Play session signing key) and DATAHUB_SYSTEM_CLIENT_SECRET (system OAuth client secret), updates every DataHub app child accordingly, and triggers a coordinated restart so the new values take effect everywhere simultaneously. USER-VISIBLE SIDE EFFECT: every active browser session is invalidated -- all currently logged-in users will be signed out and must re-login after the coordinated restart. Inter-service calls may briefly return 401 errors while the rotation is in flight. DATAHUB_SYSTEM_CLIENT_ID is the fixed identifier &quot;__datahub_system&quot; and is intentionally left untouched.</p>

<h3 id="rotate-datahub-internal-authentication-secrets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|

```json
    {

      "status": 0
    }

    "group": "string"
  }
}
```

## Rotate the DataHub secret-service encryption key

<a id="opIdServiceDataHubRotateSecretServiceEncryptionKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/rotate-secret-service-encryption-key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/rotate-secret-service-encryption-key`

<p>Generates a fresh SECRET_SERVICE_ENCRYPTION_KEY (the key GMS uses to encrypt ingestion source credentials and other sensitive values at rest), re-encrypts every stored secret from the old key to the new one, and then restarts GMS on the new key. Because the stored secrets are migrated in place, ingestion resumes on its own after the restart. USER-VISIBLE SIDE EFFECT: none for API tokens or browser sessions. Ingestion pauses only for the duration of the GMS restart and then continues.</p>

## Rotate DataHub token-service secrets

<a id="opIdServiceDataHubRotateTokenServiceSecrets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/rotate-token-service-secrets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/rotate-token-service-secrets`

<p>Generates fresh values for DATAHUB_TOKEN_SERVICE_SIGNING_KEY (the key GMS uses to sign API access tokens) and DATAHUB_TOKEN_SERVICE_SALT (the salt behind the token revocation-check hash), updates every DataHub app child that carries them, and triggers a coordinated restart so the new values take effect everywhere simultaneously. USER-VISIBLE SIDE EFFECT: every previously issued API access token (personal access tokens, service tokens) is permanently invalidated. The tokens are stateless JWTs, so the old key and salt cannot be recovered and matching tokens cannot be reissued. Users and automations must create new API tokens through the UI or GraphQL API. Browser sessions (cookie-based) are unaffected.</p>

<h3 id="rotate-datahub-token-service-secrets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|

```json
    {
      "message": "string",

      "status": 0
    }
  ],
  "message": "string",
  "rotation": {
    "group": "string"
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "service_not_found"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

    {
```

## Update service configuration

<a id="opIdServiceUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cloud": "aws-eu-central-1",
    "cmk_id": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-12345678abcd",
    "disk_space_mb": 65536,
    "group_name": "mygroup",
    "karapace": true,
    "maintenance": {
      "dow": "sunday",
      "time": "12:30:00"
    },
    "plan": "hobbyist",
    "powered": true,
    "project_vpc_id": "1007a317-aa2a-4fb4-9056-93924c5ee46f",
    "schema_registry_authz": true,
    "tech_emails": [
      {
        "email": "jane@example.com"
      }
    ],
    "termination_protection": true,
    "user_config": {}
  }'
```

`PUT /project/{project}/service/{service_name}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cloud": "aws-eu-central-1",
  "cmk_id": "12345678-1234-1234-1234-12345678abcd",
  "disk_space_mb": 65536,
  "group_name": "mygroup",
  "karapace": true,
  "maintenance": {
    "dow": "sunday",
    "time": "12:30:00"
  },
  "plan": "hobbyist",
  "powered": true,
  "project_vpc_id": "1007a317-aa2a-4fb4-9056-93924c5ee46f",
  "schema_registry_authz": true,
  "tech_emails": [
    {
      "email": "jane@example.com"
    }
  ],
  "termination_protection": true,
  "user_config": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-service-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|allow_unclean_poweroff|query|boolean|false|Allows or disallows powering off a service if some WAL segments are not available for a future restoration of the service, which might result in data loss when powering the service back on. Note: defaults to false for PostgreSQL services.|
|body|body|[ServiceUpdateRequestBody](#schemaserviceupdaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» cloud|body|string|false|Target cloud|
|» cmk_id|body|string|false|Customer Managed Key identifier (CMK ID)|
|» disk_space_mb|body|integer|false|Megabytes of disk space for data storage|
|» group_name|body|string|false|Service group name (DEPRECATED: do not use)|
|» karapace|body|boolean|false|Switch the service to use Karapace for schema registry and REST proxy|
|» maintenance|body|object|false|Automatic maintenance settings|
|» » dow|body|string|false|Day of week for installing updates|
|» » time|body|string|false|Time for installing updates, UTC|
|» plan|body|string|false|Subscription plan|
|» powered|body|boolean|false|Power-on the service (true) or power-off (false)|
|» project_vpc_id|body|string|false|Project VPC ID|
|» schema_registry_authz|body|boolean|false|Enable or disable Schema Registry authorization|
|» tech_emails|body|[object]|false|List of service technical email addresses|
|» » email|body|string|true|User email address|
|» termination_protection|body|boolean|false|Service is protected against termination and powering off|
|» user_config|body|object|false|Service type-specific settings|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » dow|monday|
|» » dow|tuesday|
|» » dow|wednesday|
|» » dow|thursday|
|» » dow|friday|
|» » dow|saturday|
|» » dow|sunday|

|» dataset_import|body|object|false|Payload to be used with dataset_import|
|» » dataset_name|body|string|true|Name of the dataset to import to PostgreSQL database. Used with dataset_import.|
|» migration_check|body|object|false|Payload to be used with migration_check|
|» » ignore_dbs|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of databases, which should be ignored during migration (supported by MySQL and PostgreSQL only at the moment)|
|» » ignore_roles|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of database roles, which should be ignored during migration (supported by PostgreSQL only at the moment)|
|» » method|body|string|false|The migration method to be used (currently supported only by Redis, Dragonfly, MySQL and PostgreSQL service types)|

|» » source_service_name|body|string|false|Service name|

## Create a new (sub) user for service

<a id="opIdServiceUserCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/user \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "access_control": {
      "pg_allow_replication": true,
      "redis_acl_categories": [
        "+@all"
      ],
      "redis_acl_channels": [
        "some*chan"
      ],
      "redis_acl_commands": [
        "-acl"
      ],
      "redis_acl_keys": [
        "prefix_*"
      ],
      "valkey_acl_categories": [
        "+@all"
      ],
      "valkey_acl_channels": [
        "some*chan"
      ],
      "valkey_acl_commands": [
        "-acl"
      ],
      "valkey_acl_keys": [
        "prefix_*"
      ]
    },
    "authentication": "caching_sha2_password",
    "mysql_grants": [
      "SELECT",
      "DELETE"
    ],
    "username": "testuser"
  }'
```

|» » valkey_acl_keys|body|[string]|false|Key access rules|
|» authentication|body|string|false|Service specific authentication details. Currently only used for MySQL where accepted options are 'mysql_native_password' and 'caching_sha2_password', latter being default when this is not explicitly set.|

## Create an upgrade step

<a id="opIdUpgradePipelineStepCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/organization/string/upgrade-pipeline/steps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auto_validation_delay_days": 7,
    "destination_project_name": "prod-project",
    "destination_service_name": "pg-prod",
    "source_project_name": "dev-project",
    "source_service_name": "pg-dev"
  }'
```

`POST /organization/{organization_id}/upgrade-pipeline/steps`

<p>Customer must have write access to both source and destination projects (read-only is not enough). Both services must belong to the organization in the URL (and thus the same organization). Initial validation is seeded based on the destination service type pinned release.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_validation_delay_days": 7,
  "destination_project_name": "prod-project",
  "destination_service_name": "pg-prod",
  "source_project_name": "dev-project",
  "source_service_name": "pg-dev"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-upgrade-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|ID of an organization|
|body|body|[UpgradePipelineStepCreateRequestBody](#schemaupgradepipelinestepcreaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» auto_validation_delay_days|body|integer|false|Days before automatic validation (defaults to 7)|
|» destination_project_name|body|string|true|Destination project name|
|» destination_service_name|body|string|true|Destination service name|
|» source_project_name|body|string|true|Source project name|
|» source_service_name|body|string|true|Source service name|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "auto_validation_delay_days": 1,
  "destination_project_name": "string",
  "destination_service_name": "string",
  "last_validation": {
    "comment": "string",
    "validated_at": "string",
```

## Validate upgrade step

<a id="opIdUpgradePipelineStepValidate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/project/string/service/string/upgrade-validation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Validated after testing"
  }'
```

`POST /project/{project}/service/{service_name}/upgrade-validation`

<p>Validate maintenance level currently running on the given service, unblocking it for any service(s) that are targets of a upgrade pipeline step with this service as the source service. This allows the destination services of the pipeline steps to have all maintenances applied to the source service automatically applied to them.</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Validated after testing"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-upgrade-step-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project|path|string|true|Project name|
|service_name|path|string|true|Service name|
|body|body|[UpgradePipelineStepValidateRequestBody](#schemaupgradepipelinestepvalidaterequestbody)|false|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Validation comment|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "project_not_found"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "upgrade_step_validation_not_possible_due_to_service_state"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="validate-upgrade-step-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Validate upgrade step|None|
|404|Not Found|Project not found|Inline|
|409|Conflict|Validation not possible due to state of the service|Inline|

<h3 id="validate-upgrade-step-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## Create new access token

<a id="opIdAccessTokenCreate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/access_token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Integration client Alpha",
    "extend_when_used": true,
    "ip_allowlist": [
      "192.168.6.0/24"
    ],
    "max_age_seconds": 86400,
    "scopes": [
      "user:read"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /access_token`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Integration client Alpha",
  "extend_when_used": true,
  "ip_allowlist": [
    "192.168.6.0/24"
  ],
  "max_age_seconds": 86400,
  "scopes": [
    "user:read"
  ]
}
```

|» description|body|string|true|Name / description of an access token|
|» extend_when_used|body|boolean|false|Extend token expiration time when token is used. Only applicable if max_age_seconds is specified.|
|» ip_allowlist|body|[string]|false|List of allowed IP ranges|
|» max_age_seconds|body|number|false|Time the token remains valid since creation (or since last use if extend_when_used is true)|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Scopes this token is restricted to, if specified|

> Example responses

```json
      "message": "string",

      "status": 0
    }
  ],
  "expiry_time": "string",
  "extend_when_used": true,

  ],

}
```

## Authenticate user

<a id="opIdUserAuth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.aiven.io/userauth \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "otp": "987654",
    "password": "!@$password12345"
  }'
```

`POST /userauth`

<p>Authenticate user and return token for following authorizations</p>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "otp": "987654",
  "password": "!@$password12345"
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserAuthRequestBody](#schemauserauthrequestbody)|false|none|
|» email|body|string|true|User email address|
|» otp|body|string|false|One-time password|
|» password|body|string|true|User password|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "more_info": "string",
      "status": 0
    }
  ],
  "message": "string",
  "return_url": "string",
  "state": "string",
  "tenant": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "user_email": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "errors": [
    {
      "message": "string",
      "error_code": "user_deactivated"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="authenticate-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response|[UserAuthResponse](#schemauserauthresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Operation not allowed|Inline|

<h3 id="authenticate-user-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **403**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message|string|false|none|none|
|errors|[object]|false|none|none|
|» message|string|false|none|none|
|» error_code|string|false|none|user_deactivated: Your account has been temporary suspended. Please contact your organization admin.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» error_code|user_deactivated|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

ServiceKafkaQuotaCreateRequestBody

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client\-id|string|false|none|Represents a logical group of clients, assigned a unique name by the client application. Quotas can be applied based on user, client-id, or both. The most relevant quota is chosen for each connection. All connections within a quota group share the same quota.|
|consumer_byte_rate|number|false|none|Defines the bandwidth limit in bytes/sec for each group of clients sharing a quota. Every distinct client group is allocated a specific quota, as defined by the cluster, on a per-broker basis. Exceeding this limit results in client throttling.|
|producer_byte_rate|number|false|none|Defines the bandwidth limit in bytes/sec for each group of clients sharing a quota. Every distinct client group is allocated a specific quota, as defined by the cluster, on a per-broker basis. Exceeding this limit results in client throttling.|
|request_percentage|number|false|none|Sets the maximum percentage of CPU time that a client group can use on request handler I/O and network threads per broker within a quota window. Exceeding this limit triggers throttling. The quota, expressed as a percentage, also indicates the total allowable CPU usage for the client groups sharing the quota.|
|user|string|false|none|Represents a logical group of clients, assigned a unique name by the client application. Quotas can be applied based on user, client-id, or both. The most relevant quota is chosen for each connection. All connections within a quota group share the same quota.|

ServiceKafkaTopicCreateRequestBody

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cleanup_policy|string|false|none|The retention policy to use on old segments. Possible values include 'delete', 'compact', or a comma-separated list of them. The default policy ('delete') will discard old segments when their retention time or size limit has been reached. The 'compact' setting will enable log compaction on the topic.|
|config|object|false|none|Kafka topic configuration|
|min_insync_replicas|integer|false|none|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|owner_user_group_id|string|false|none|The user group that owns this topic|
|partitions|integer|false|none|Number of partitions|
|replication|integer|false|none|Number of replicas|
|retention_bytes|integer|false|none|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|retention_hours|integer|false|none|DEPRECATED: use config.retention_ms|
|tags|[object]|false|none|Topic tags|
|topic_description|string|false|none|Topic description|
|topic_name|string|true|none|Topic name|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cleanup_policy|delete|
|cleanup_policy|compact|
|cleanup_policy|compact,delete|

ServiceKafkaTopicUpdateRequestBody

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config|object|false|none|Kafka topic configuration|
|min_insync_replicas|integer|false|none|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), this configuration specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful. If this minimum cannot be met, then the producer will raise an exception (either NotEnoughReplicas or NotEnoughReplicasAfterAppend). When used together, min.insync.replicas and acks allow you to enforce greater durability guarantees. A typical scenario would be to create a topic with a replication factor of 3, set min.insync.replicas to 2, and produce with acks of 'all'. This will ensure that the producer raises an exception if a majority of replicas do not receive a write.|
|owner_user_group_id|string|false|none|The user group that owns this topic|
|partitions|integer|false|none|Number of partitions|
|replication|integer|false|none|Number of replicas|
|retention_bytes|integer|false|none|This configuration controls the maximum size a partition (which consists of log segments) can grow to before we will discard old log segments to free up space if we are using the 'delete' retention policy. By default there is no size limit only a time limit. Since this limit is enforced at the partition level, multiply it by the number of partitions to compute the topic retention in bytes.|
|retention_hours|integer|false|none|DEPRECATED: use config.retention_ms|
|tags|[object]|false|none|Topic tags|
|topic_description|string|false|none|Topic description|

ServiceKafkaMirrorMakerCreateReplicationFlowRequestBody

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config_properties_exclude|string|false|none|A comma separated list of topic configuration properties and/or regexes that should not be replicated. If omitted, MirrorMaker will use default list of exclusions. For stability reasons, we always include the unclean.leader.election.enable field in the excluded parameters. If you have specific requirements for this configuration, please reach out to our support team for assistance.|
|diskless_az_enabled|boolean|false|none|Adds a diskless_az= hint to the replication flow's Kafka client.id so that diskless Kafka clusters serve the flow from brokers in the same availability zone.|
|emit_backward_heartbeats_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to emit heartbeats to the direction opposite to the flow, i.e. to the source cluster|
|emit_heartbeats_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to emit heartbeats to the target cluster|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Is replication flow enabled|
|exactly_once_delivery_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to enable exactly-once message delivery. We recommend you set this to enabled for new replications.|
|follower_fetching_enabled|boolean|false|none|Assigns a Rack ID based on the availability-zone to enable follower fetching and rack awareness per replication flow.|
|offset_lag_max|integer|false|none|How out-of-sync a remote partition can be before it is resynced (default: 100)|
|offset_syncs_topic_location|string|false|none|The location of the offset-syncs topic|
|replication_factor|integer|false|none|Replication factor used when creating the remote topics. If the replication factor surpasses the number of nodes in the target cluster, topic creation will fail.|
|replication_policy_class|string|false|none|Class which defines the remote topic naming convention|
|source_cluster|string|true|none|The alias of the source cluster to use in this replication flow. Can contain the following symbols: ASCII alphanumerics, '.', '_', and '-'.|
|sync_group_offsets_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether to periodically write the translated offsets of replicated consumer groups (in the source cluster) to __consumer_offsets topic in target cluster, as long as no active consumers in that group are connected to the target cluster|
|sync_group_offsets_interval_seconds|integer|false|none|Frequency at which consumer group offsets are synced (default: 60, every minute)|
|target_cluster|string|true|none|The alias of the target cluster to use in this replication flow. Can contain the following symbols: ASCII alphanumerics, '.', '_', and '-'.|
|topics|[string]|false|none|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should be replicated. MirrorMaker will replicate these topics if they are not matched by &quot;topics.exclude&quot;. Currently defaults to [&quot;.*&quot;].|
|topics.blacklist|[string]|false|none|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|
|topics.exclude|[string]|false|none|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|
|topics_exclude|[string]|false|none|Topic names and regular expressions that match topic names that should not be replicated. MirrorMaker will not replicate these topics even if they are matched by &quot;topics&quot;. If not set, MM2 uses the default exclusion.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|offset_syncs_topic_location|source|
|offset_syncs_topic_location|target|
|replication_policy_class|org.apache.kafka.connect.mirror.DefaultReplicationPolicy|
|replication_policy_class|org.apache.kafka.connect.mirror.IdentityReplicationPolicy|
